purpose: Cross-environment defensive comparison of censorship/control mechanisms across DNS, TLS/SNI, TCP RST, throttling, full shutdown, allowlist, routing capture, and RF/GNSS. Distinguish generic mechanism families from vendor-specific fingerprints and from foreign control-plane attribution.

headline.main_result: Post-ClientHello timeout/RST behavior is a DPI-family signature, not a vendor-unique signature.
headline.reason: No current foreign event yet combines reproducible path-specific interference, provider-side negative controls, ASN/hop localization, independent replication, and a specific device/vendor/control-channel causal bridge.

examples: France/New Caledonia 2024: selective TikTok restriction through local operator context; politically targeted restriction without TSPU-like packet fingerprint.
Türkiye 2024-2025: censorship IP 195.175.254.2 returned on multiple networks for Instagram/Boykotyap/Discord-related blocking.
India 2026: Telegram blocking on some networks via censorship-associated DNS answers.
Albania 2025: TikTok DNS tampering via NXDOMAIN on Vodafone networks.
DNS_BLOCKING.inference: DNS manipulation is common and technologically non-specific. Similar political outcomes can arise with no DPI/RST involvement.

examples: Kyrgyzstan/MegaCom AS50223 2024: TikTok blocking observed with TLS session timeout after ClientHello; PROTEI DPI deployment is historically confirmed on MegaCom, but interference occurred on multiple Kyrgyz networks and AS50223 had Rostelecom upstream dependency.
Russia 2024-2026: Discord commonly times out after first TLS write; Bluesky shows either TLS timeout or injected RST immediately after ClientHello across many networks.
Saudi Arabia/Mobily AS35819 2026: Tinder selectively blocked by injected RST after ClientHello while DNS and initial TCP connection succeed.
Türkiye 2024: Discord measurements include connection resets after first TLS write, alongside independent DNS censorship fingerprints.
TLS_POST_CLIENTHELLO_INTERFERENCE.inference: timeout/RST after ClientHello is a broad SNI/DPI mechanism family and cannot identify PROTEI, RDP/TSPU, or any other vendor by itself.

examples: Cuba 2017: OONI measured injected TCP RST and used latency/TTL behavior to infer a middlebox path for blocked services.
Cuba 2021: Signal/TLS connection-reset behavior consistent with SNI-targeting DPI during protest-period restrictions.
Russia 2026: Bluesky sometimes receives RST immediately after ClientHello.
Saudi Arabia 2026: Mobily/Tinder receives RST after ClientHello.
RST_INJECTION.inference: RST alone is generic. Vendor attribution requires lower-level distinguishing properties such as reproducible TTL/IPID/sequence/timing/source characteristics plus known-device controls.

examples: Türkiye 2023: Twitter restriction showed TLS handshake latency rising from roughly tens of milliseconds to multiple seconds on several ASNs, while control endpoints did not show the same pattern.
Russia: TSPU-related censorship history includes centrally coordinated throttling and newer selective transfer disruption patterns.
THROTTLING.inference: Performance degradation needs matched endpoint and path controls; generic packet loss or congestion is insufficient.

examples: Uganda 2026 election: nationwide Internet shutdown from 13-18 January confirmed by IODA, Cloudflare Radar and Google traffic; regulator directive contained an exclusion list for essential healthcare, banking and government systems. After restoration, social-media blocking remained.
Belarus 2025 election: order to restrict websites hosted outside .by effectively blocked most foreign websites while domestic namespace remained available.
Cuba: repeated event-conditioned national/regional outages occur in a highly centralized state-monopoly access environment.
FULL_SHUTDOWN_AND_ALLOWLIST.inference: deny-except-allowlist is an important functional analog to Russian whitelist modes but does not imply shared technology or foreign control.

examples: Occupied Ukraine 2022: Cloudflare tracked more than 20 Ukrainian networks whose routing shifted to Russian ISPs; affected traffic became subject to Russian controls, surveillance and censorship.
MegaCom AS50223 2024: Cloudflare listed Rostelecom AS12389 as the sole upstream, creating a strong localization confound for censorship measurements observed from inside AS50223.
ROUTING_AND_TRANSIT_CAPTURE.inference: An OONI probe ASN is not automatically the physical location of interference. Upstream path localization is mandatory before vendor attribution.

examples: Serbia 15 March 2025 and 23 May 2026 protest-related periods: BIRN identified GNSS jamming/spoofing signals using GPSWise/GPSJam and aviation/drone observations.
RF_GNSS.inference: RF/GNSS interference is a separate physical-layer mechanism and must never be merged into DPI/TSPU attribution without direct evidence.

country_core_matrix.Belarus: STRONG_POSITIVE_CONTROL for centralized protest/election-conditioned restrictions and external-vs-domestic selective access.
country_core_matrix.Cuba: STRONG_POSITIVE_CONTROL plus Russian SORM/PROTEI vendor-lineage bridge; measured RST/DPI exists but causal link to specific PROTEI DPI device remains open.
country_core_matrix.Kazakhstan: ORANGE path-control candidate; historical interception and protest-conditioned degradation are strong, 2026 ASN/path mechanism still incomplete.
country_core_matrix.Georgia: NEGATIVE protest-shutdown control; severe protest repression without stable shutdown pattern.
country_core_matrix.Serbia: NEGATIVE Internet-shutdown control plus separate RF/GNSS signal.
country_core_matrix.France/New Caledonia: DNS/selective-block negative technology control: political selective restriction can occur without RST/TLS/TSPU-like fingerprint.

global_external_controls.Uganda: Full shutdown plus explicit exclusion list/allowlist; proves functional deny-except-allowlist is not uniquely Russian.
global_external_controls.Türkiye: Independent DNS, RST, and throttling mechanisms; same-day Discord blocking with Russia is a negative control against timing-only attribution.
global_external_controls.Saudi_Arabia: Clean independent example of RST-after-ClientHello DPI on one ASN; destroys vendor uniqueness of that broad fingerprint.
global_external_controls.India_Albania: DNS manipulation controls showing distinct blocking implementations.
global_external_controls.Occupied_Ukraine: Positive routing-control example where path jurisdiction change directly altered censorship/control environment.

fingerprint_hierarchy.LEVEL_2_GENERIC_MECHANISM: DNS tamper / TLS timeout / RST / throttling / shutdown. Identifies mechanism family only.
fingerprint_hierarchy.LEVEL_3_PATH_LOCALIZATION: ASN/hop localization with matched bypass or alternate-path control. Stronger but still not vendor identity.
fingerprint_hierarchy.LEVEL_4_LOW_LEVEL_PACKET_SIGNATURE: Stable RST TTL, IPID, seq/ack behavior, timing, direction, handshake phase, QUIC-vs-TCP behavior, and repeatability across known deployments.
fingerprint_hierarchy.LEVEL_5_VENDOR_CAUSAL_BRIDGE: Known device/product on the path plus matching signature or configuration/management evidence.
fingerprint_hierarchy.LEVEL_6_CONTROL_CHANNEL: Specific operator/vendor management or remote-control channel tied to the event. Required for foreign remote-control attribution.

current_best_tests: MegaCom: compare raw OONI measurements across AS50223 and other Kyrgyz ASNs for the same TikTok endpoints to determine whether AS50223 has a distinct packet/error profile.
Cuba: compare 2017 and 2021 reset behavior by TTL/IPID/latency/handshake phase to test whether the same middlebox family persisted.

Russia: use known TSPU measurements as a mechanism reference, not a vendor identity template; include QUIC SNI behavior as an additional dimension because TSPU has documented SNI-dependent QUIC censorship.
Kazakhstan: prioritize route/ASN localization of current anomalies and alternate-path controls.
Belarus/Uganda/France: preserve as functional and mechanism-specific negative/positive controls to prevent over-attribution.
Serbia: keep GNSS completely separated from Internet-control scoring.
epistemic_firewall: same product family != same device instance
same device family != same control channel
Russian-origin vendor presence != Russian remote command
temporal coincidence alone = zero attribution weight
